sources.title: Final UK greenhouse gas emissions statistics: 1990 to 2024
2024 UK Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Final Figures - statistical release

guard_patterns.handling: Keep UK territorial inventory scope and sector boundary explicit.
Keep the published inventory methodology and data-source lineage.
Keep MtCO2e, gas, fuel, activity and modelling bases explicit.
Use the final 1990-2024 inventory; do not substitute older estimates.
Do not convert national inventory methodology to site or parcel measurements.
Never infer a parcel emission value from national inventory methods.
Require explicit PASS review for each generated control.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory solid-waste GDP-proxy methodology QA
facts: The 1990-2024 final inventory changed the landfill model used for solid-waste emissions.
Gross GDP data are now used as a proxy for solid-waste disposal volumes where actual activity data are unavailable.
Historic solid-waste disposal activity data are uncertain and unavailable before 1997.
The previous method extrapolated 1990-1996 disposal volumes from 1997 using household and employment statistics.
An external review found the previous proxy approach inconsistent with IPCC inventory guidance.
The GDP-proxy change was introduced to improve consistency with IPCC guidance.
The methodological change is confined to the waste sector.
The revised method produces a large decrease in landfill-emissions estimates in the early historic time series.
The final 2024 release applies inventory method improvements back through the historical series rather than only to 2024.
National landfill-model estimates must not be interpreted as local-site or parcel measurements.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory domestic-wastewater IPCC-2019 methodology QA
facts: The domestic-wastewater model was revised in the 1990-2024 final inventory.
The revision was designed to improve consistency with IPCC guidance and capture UK-specific wastewater-treatment practices.
An external review identified inconsistencies in the previous wastewater model.
The revised model uses parameters and emission factors from the 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines.
UK-specific assumptions are used for processes not covered by IPCC guidance.
Academic literature supplements the model for treatment processes not fully covered by IPCC guidance.
The change is exclusive to the waste sector.
The revision increases domestic-wastewater emissions estimates across the historic time series.
The increase is driven mainly by higher nitrous-oxide estimates.
The revised national wastewater model is an inventory estimate and not a direct measurement of an individual treatment site.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory domestic-shipping DUKES-normalisation QA
facts: The domestic-shipping emissions model was revised for the 1990-2024 final inventory.
Ship-movement estimates are now normalised against DUKES fuel-sales data.
Previously, domestic-shipping emissions estimates were based on ship movements without this DUKES normalisation.
The previous movement-only approach produced inconsistency with DUKES fuel-use totals.
Modelled ship-movement emissions are now adjusted to match the total fuel use implied by DUKES sales.
The same normalisation is applied to modelled inland-waterway emissions.
The same normalisation is applied to modelled port-machinery emissions.
Naval shipping is excluded from this normalisation because it is based on Ministry of Defence fuel purchases.
The shipping-method changes reduce UK domestic-shipping emissions estimates across the historic time series.
The normalised model remains a national inventory method and does not establish vessel-level or parcel-level emissions.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory global-AIS shipping coverage QA
facts: The shipping model incorporates global Automatic Identification System data from 2019.
The previous model used UK AIS data from 2014.
Global AIS data improve the modelling and coverage of shipping activities.
The improved AIS coverage contributes to revised domestic-shipping emissions estimates.
The global AIS update also improves coverage of activities in Crown Dependencies and Overseas Territories.
The UK domestic-shipping revisions decrease estimates across the historic time series overall.
The Crown Dependencies and Overseas Territories revisions can move differently from the UK revision.
The final release reports that improved coverage raises modeled domestic-shipping emissions for Crown Dependencies and Overseas Territories across the historic series.
Revisions for Crown Dependencies and Overseas Territories are excluded from the UK-total impacts table.
AIS-based inventory modelling must not be treated as a direct measurement of emissions from an individual voyage.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory shipping at-berth double-count QA
facts: The shipping model was updated to remove double counting of at-berth emissions.
Previously, at-berth emissions were reported in both domestic and international shipping totals.
IPCC guidance requires at-berth emissions to be reported against domestic shipping.
Under the revised method all at-berth emissions are included within domestic-shipping emissions only.
Removing the double count reduces UK-based international-shipping emissions estimates across the time series.
International-shipping emissions are excluded from the UK territorial total under IPCC reporting rules.
International-shipping emissions are nevertheless reported separately as a memorandum item.
International-shipping emissions are included in Carbon Budget 6 accounting as stated by the final release.
Revisions to international-shipping emissions are therefore excluded from the UK-total impacts table.
The domestic-versus-international accounting boundary must be preserved when reusing these figures.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory industrial-wastewater CRT inclusion QA
facts: Industrial-wastewater discharge emissions are included in UK totals for the first time in the 1990-2024 final inventory.
They had previously been excluded because the 2006 IPCC Guidelines lacked relevant guidance.
The 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines introduced relevant guidance.
The source was added to the common reporting table format used for Paris Agreement reporting.
Its addition to the CRT supports inclusion of the source in the national inventory totals.
The change is exclusive to the waste sector.
The new source increases nitrous-oxide emissions across the historic time series.
The new source also increases methane emissions across the historic time series.
The reported impact on the national total is small relative to major inventory sectors.
Industrial-wastewater inventory estimates are not direct measurements for individual industrial sites.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory biogas and natural-gas separation QA
facts: Biogas and natural-gas use from the gas distribution network are separated for the first time in the final inventory.
Previously, biogas in the gas network was treated as a component of natural gas and was not distinguishable.
An external review identified lack of transparency in the previous treatment.
DUKES data on biogas injection into the gas distribution network are used in the revised method.
The revised method produces separate estimates for fossil-fuel and biofuel-use emissions.
Almost all biogas and natural-gas blending occurs in the gas distribution network.
Consumers with more direct gas supply, such as some large-scale consumers or upstream oil and gas sites, are treated as using natural gas only.
Gas-use apportionment was revised across industry, fuel supply, electricity supply, domestic transport, buildings and product uses, and agriculture.
The total UK emissions impact of the biogas separation is small even though sector allocation changes.
The sector-apportionment change must not be interpreted as evidence about the fuel mix of a specific parcel or facility without site data.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory iron-and-steel five-year-average QA
facts: The iron-and-steel emissions method was revised in the 1990-2024 final inventory.
A five-year average is applied to fuel data for 2022, 2023 and 2024.
The previous method used annual fuel data to estimate iron-and-steel production emissions.
Recent coke-oven closures made the previous annual tracking method difficult to justify.
After those closures the UK iron-and-steel industry relied on imported coke.
UK coke-oven coke data therefore ceased to be a valid standalone tracker for sector emissions.
Alignment between the previous method and operator ETS data had deteriorated.
The five-year average improves alignment with ETS data.
The change is exclusive to the industry sector and decreases estimates for 2022 and 2023.
The averaging method is a national inventory estimation adjustment, not a substitute for operator-specific verified emissions.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory gas-oil time-series consistency QA
facts: Gas-oil emissions estimates were revised to improve time-series consistency.
DUKES can revise gas-oil data back to 2009 and the inventory incorporates those revisions.
DUKES revisions can create a discontinuity between 2008 and 2009 in the inventory input series.
Additional inconsistencies exist before 1997 because older DUKES data are not electronically available.
Domestic, commercial and agricultural 1998-2008 activity data are interpolated from 1997 and 2009 DUKES data.
Several industrial 1990-1997 activity series are extrapolated from DUKES data from 1998 onward.
Other industrial and unclassified 1990-2008 activity series are extrapolated from 2009 onward.
Forest-machinery activity uses forestry statistics instead of DUKES data.
Overall gas-oil emissions remain consistent with DUKES total gas-oil use.
The revisions mainly alter sector apportionment among industry, agriculture, and buildings and product uses rather than the overall gas-oil total.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory peat calorific-value and carbon-content QA
facts: Peat-fuel emissions estimates were revised to better reflect UK use cases.
The revision responded to recommendations from a review of the peat-emissions model.
A higher calorific value for peat is used in place of the IPCC default value.
The revised calorific value changes the conversion between peat activity and energy/emissions estimates.
The carbon content assigned to fuel peat extracted from Northern Ireland was increased.
The Northern Ireland carbon-content update aligns the inventory with UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology estimates.
The peat revision is exclusive to the buildings and product uses sector.
The change produces a small increase in emissions across the historic time series.
The revised peat factors are inventory assumptions and not measurements of individual peat batches.
UK-specific calorific-value and carbon-content provenance must be preserved when comparing old and new peat estimates.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory fluoropolymer HFC inclusion QA
facts: Hydrofluorocarbon emissions from fluoropolymer production are included in the national totals for the first time.
The estimates use Pollution Inventory data.
Additional site-level data from the Environment Agency are also used.
The new source is assigned to the industry sector.
The change causes a small increase in national HFC emissions estimates.
HFC-23 is among the fluoropolymer-production gases explicitly added.
HFC-32 is among the fluoropolymer-production gases explicitly added.
HFC-125 is among the fluoropolymer-production gases explicitly added.
The new fluoropolymer estimates are part of the revised historic inventory methodology.
National fluoropolymer totals must not be converted into parcel-level emissions without verified facility-specific evidence.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory domestic-wood HDD and stock-effects QA
facts: Domestic wood-combustion emissions estimates were revised in the final inventory.
The revised method uses new DUKES data on changes in domestic wood use attributable to heating degree days.
The revised method also uses DUKES information on stock impacts affecting domestic wood use.
Previously, HDD-related wood-use changes were inferred using adjusted domestic-gas use.
Previously, unadjusted domestic-gas use also formed part of that proxy approach.
The gas-based proxy was replaced by a direct breakdown of impacts on domestic wood use.
The change is exclusive to the buildings and product uses sector.
The final release reports a small decrease in emissions in 2023 from this method change.
Heating-degree-day effects are a methodological input rather than a direct measurement of emissions from an individual home.
The direct DUKES wood-use breakdown should be preserved instead of reverting to the earlier gas-proxy method.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory agriculture dairy-cattle and LESSE QA
facts: The dairy-cattle emissions model was updated to use the latest slaughter-weight data to derive cattle weight.
The cattle-weight update increases estimated enteric methane emissions.
The cattle-weight update also causes a small increase in nitrous-oxide emissions from dairy cattle.
The slurry-management model was updated for low-emissions slurry spreading equipment uptake.
Country-specific LESSE uptake data are used for cattle and pig slurry in England.
Great Britain data are used to estimate LESSE uptake in Wales.
Great Britain data are used to estimate LESSE uptake in Scotland.
Great Britain data are used to estimate LESSE uptake in Northern Ireland.
The LESSE-method update has a negligible impact on total emissions estimates.
These agriculture model updates are national or country-scale inventory methods and not farm-level measurements.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory agriculture grassland ammonia and sheep QA
facts: The grassland model includes new assumptions reflecting improved grass yield and nitrogen uptake from plant breeding.
The grassland revision produces a negligible increase in nitrous-oxide emissions from grass-residue decomposition.
The grassland revision decreases nitrous-oxide emissions from leaching of applied fertiliser, manures and excreta.
A new method estimates ammonia emissions from decomposition of plant residues on the soil surface.
Ammonia is treated as an air pollutant rather than a greenhouse gas.
Ammonia deposition nevertheless acts as an indirect source of nitrous-oxide emissions.
The new ammonia method causes a small increase in nitrous-oxide emissions from grassland deposition.
The sheep model uses grass-energy-content assumptions that better reflect survey evidence.
The revised sheep energy assumption increases grass intake and enteric methane while revised crude-protein assumptions reduce grass nitrogen content over time.
The sheep revision increases nitrous-oxide emissions early in the time series but decreases them in recent years.

packages.title: 2026 final-inventory LULUCF forest peatland and cropland QA
facts: The forest-carbon model was updated to better reflect tree species and growth rates for afforestation from 2011.
The forest update includes deadwood from natural competition among young trees.
The forest update improves estimation of carbon transfer from branches on dead trees into soil.
The forest update improves consistency with wood-production estimates.
New forest-planting and wood-production activity data were incorporated.
Together the forest changes reduce net forestry and harvested-wood-products emissions across the time series.
Peatland modelling incorporates evidence from Defra-funded studies of historic domestic peat-extraction areas.
Peatland modelling incorporates Defra rewetting data for 2021-2024 and the Peatland ACTION programme for Scotland, reducing net emissions slightly.
Cropland and biomass carbon-stock modelling incorporates the 2024 Agricultural Census for England.
The cropland update produces a small increase in net emissions across the time series.
